When someone asks me if they should just use the Wix AI builder instead of paying for a website, my answer is always the same: go for it, if it fits.

An AI website builder is a fair choice if you're comfortable with tech and need a simple site of one to three pages. Past that, the AI only does the easy part. The setup, the SEO basics, the domain and hosting, and checking every line it wrote are still on you.

I broke down when each option makes sense, what to add up on cost, and what happens if you want to move off a builder later:
https://brightboxdigital.io/blog/ai-website-builder-vs-professional-website-development/

#WebDesign #SmallBusiness #FortWayne

AI website builder or hire a professional?

If you're tech savvy and need one to three pages, an AI builder can work. I mean that.

If your website needs to bring in calls and quote requests, the AI only does the first part of the job. Setup, SEO and fact-checking the copy are still yours.

Full breakdown at the link in bio.

#WebDesign #AIWebsiteBuilder #SmallBusinessMarketing #FortWayneBusiness #WebsiteTips

Every website builder now leads with the same pitch: describe your business and get a site in minutes.

I tell business owners they're welcome to try it. I use AI builders myself to put together mock-ups for clients.

But for a business that needs its website to bring in leads, the AI is the easy part. The time goes into everything around it: setup, SEO basics, domain and hosting, and checking the copy. Google's own guidance says AI-generated content, including page titles and meta descriptions, should be fact-checked by a person before it goes live.

Two things owners often find out later: without code you're limited to the platform's layouts, and a Wix site can't be moved to another host.
